coverage.samplingNote: Curated current families and fixed shapes, with a small explicit legal flex grid. Counts do not describe all possible configurable machines.
coverage.memoryUnitBasis: Provider-published GB retained without numerical conversion. Oracle does not specify the byte convention on the shape page; the legacy GiB field holds this nominal capacity, not a verified binary-byte measurement.
exclusions: Retired P100 and previous-generation CPU shapes
Sales-contact-only HPC and dense-I/O E5/E6 shapes
GB200/GB300/B300/MI355X shapes with inconsistent published memory capacities
Spot, commitments, negotiated prices, dedicated VM hosts, Windows and AI Enterprise license add-ons

coverage.scope: Dallas public USD full-share multi-tenant Linux base rates, exact named ordinary-access profiles. Snapshot rows retain their actual deployment-fetch timestamps.

benchmarkMethodology.name: Exact-shape measured CPU references
benchmarkMethodology.selection: First valid exact provider/shape CPU result, checking listed datasets in order.

datasets.name: Original measured Geekbench 6 multicore cloud-VM results
datasets.selection: One currently published successful Linux CPU task per provider and exact server API reference, at the pinned repository commit. No extrapolation across VM sizes or processors.
datasets.hardwareVerification: Thread count must match nominal vCPUs where catalog specs exist. Reported guest memory must be within 15% plus 0.35 GiB below nominal, or at most 5% above. Provider and exact VM API name are the original author's repository path. An AWS model that names an EC2 shape must match; older Xen models are generic. Rows without nominal specifications are retained with nominalSpecsVerified=false and ramGiB=null; exclude these until joined and verified.
datasets.scoreVerification: Positive finite multicore score from original results.json; cross-checked against stdout summary wherever present. AArch64 Preview output may omit the summary. Task must have exit_code=0 and no error.
datasets.limitation: Historical single runs by Spare Cores, not provider performance guarantees, repeated-trial estimates, sustained-load guarantees or measurements from the selected pricing region. Test software, host CPUs and dates vary. Current Inspector configuration skips Geekbench on hosts above 32 CPUs and sets a container memory limit to 85% of host memory; historical configurations vary. Mismatched CPU topology is excluded rather than scaled. Original task timestamps have no timezone and are preserved without inventing one.
datasets.sourceLinks: Commit-pinned original benchmark-author output. Upstream placeholder Geekbench Browser upload URLs are deliberately not used.

datasets.name: Exact-cloud-configuration Geekbench 6 CPU reference measurements
datasets.selection: One curated, publicly verifiable Linux multi-core result per exact instance shape; observed topology and memory checked against nominal VM specifications. No scaling across sizes or substitute processor models. Original benchmark version, edition and date retained.
datasets.compatibility: Geekbench 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 CPU scores are comparable for systems without SME per Primate Labs; 6.0 is excluded. AArch64 Preview editions are retained and disclosed, with historical runtime and hardware variability.
datasets.limitations: Community-submitted historical single runs are not controlled replications, random sampling, provider performance guarantees, or measurements of the current price region. Unknown regions are null. Nominal RAM differs from guest-available memory. Discovery favors publicly indexed AWS model names; provider coverage is incomplete.

gpuBenchmarkMethodology.formula: GPU price = full instance USD/hour / (Geekbench 6 OpenCL score / 1000)
gpuBenchmarkMethodology.unit: USD per hour per 1,000 Geekbench 6 OpenCL points
gpuBenchmarkMethodology.selection: Public Geekbench 6.3.0 OpenCL Linux results naming the exact AWS VM shape, with matching vCPU count, plausible available RAM and the allocated GPU. Only instances with exactly one allocated GPU qualify. Scores are measurements, not GPU-model proxies or extrapolations.
gpuBenchmarkMethodology.coverage: Two verified AWS T4 shapes. No exact-shape Geekbench 7 OpenCL result was verified in this search. Missing scores remain missing. This sparse sample cannot support a large multivariable model of cloud GPU prices.
gpuBenchmarkMethodology.limitations: One historical community submission per shape, with undisclosed benchmark region. Different drivers, distributions and host conditions affect scores. Geekbench OpenCL is a general GPU-compute benchmark, not an LLM throughput or training metric. CPU and GPU scores are distinct scales. Do not mix these results with Geekbench 7 GPU-model chart scores.

coverage.sampling: AWS non-burstable Linux regional on-demand shapes; Azure East US Linux meters matched to exact hardware metadata; Google Iowa predefined compute and network tables plus documented N1 GPU bundles; Alibaba Virginia public ECS catalog; Oracle fixed shapes and a disclosed representative flexible-VM sample; IBM Dallas public VPC profiles.
coverage.exclusions: AWS T-family and Azure burstable instances; Spot/reserved/commitment/promotion/licensed OS prices; Azure shapes without active exact hardware metadata or with ambiguous Linux meters; Google shared-core/sole-tenant/custom shapes and tables without an explicit Iowa region; unverified or unavailable public regional prices. Provider-specific exclusions accompany each source.
coverage.limitations: This is a catalog of public list rates, not a capacity guarantee. Distinct disk variants and VM sizes remain separate priced shapes. Catalog count is not benchmark-matched training count. Accelerator ASIC/FPGA/media instances are identified separately from GPUs.

attributions.name: Spare Cores hardware metadata
attributions.changes: Selected exact server identifiers, nominal CPU/RAM and accelerator fields. Converted memory_amount and gpu_memory_total from MiB to GiB. Records retain upstream lifecycle state and CPU allocation type. No performance scores inferred.

attributions.name: Spare Cores cloud server benchmark measurements
attributions.changes: Selected AWS, Azure and GCP Linux Geekbench CPU task results; parsed scores, metadata and hardware; joined nominal public catalog specifications; rejected incomplete, failed and mismatched runs. No scores estimated or rescaled.

memoryUnitConvention: Memory uses documented GiB where available. New catalog rows whose providers specify nominal GB without a byte convention retain that value and an explicit ramUnit/vramUnit of GB; no decimal conversion is assumed. Original capacities and units are retained. Source memory definitions are preserved: Google Cloud defines its GB as binary GiB; explicitly decimal GB elsewhere are converted using 1 GB = 10^9 bytes, while GiB use 2^30 bytes. Provider memory-label conventions may differ, so a normalized nominal figure does not prove a difference in usable device memory.
scope: One US reference region per provider; Linux, public on-demand USD/hour. CPU and RAM are published hardware specifications, not performance estimates. Azure hardware metadata is adapted from Spare Cores under CC BY-SA 4.0; rates remain official Microsoft prices. Google Cloud CPU/RAM and rates come from official predefined VM tables; N1 GPU configurations add the independently published GPU charge to the full VM rate. Alibaba, Oracle and IBM prices come from their public pricing catalogs. Oracle flexible rates compose published CPU and RAM components; selected flexible configurations are a representative sample. Full machine prices include bundled storage/transfer where applicable; separate disks, egress, public IPv4, tax and support are excluded.
